contract.note: Treating news fact-finding as research is ordinary. Testing whole answers for false or fabricated content fairly assesses the explicit universal claim.

evidence.note: The dated report describes journalist-reviewed whole answers. Approximately 9% had no issues, contradicting the universal assertion under the contract.

Only 19% of answers citing BBC content introduced factual errors. This supports contradiction within that subset, although the separate quotation findings limit the inferred 81% hallucination-free figure.
A participating broadcaster reports substantial significant and major issues. These thresholds cannot establish whether the remaining answers contained minor hallucinations.

reviews.rationale: The expert review found a meaningful share of whole answers without any identified issues. That contradicts the categorical claim. Frequent errors support a reliability warning but do not establish that every research answer contains hallucinations.

contract.note: The contract narrows any slowdown to a sustained slowdown that takes revenue off the required path. The speaker supplied neither restriction. This changes which events activate the conditional.
